Nobody at {settlement} calls it a breach and nobody ever had to: the wagons came a little short and then a little shorter, through {timeband_span}, and the clerks weighed what arrived against what was promised until the ledger would not close.
The {route} is open again, to anything at all; where a treaty stood there is distance and custom now, and custom binds nobody.
The {term} is {timeband_age} and no hand that signed it still holds a seat; the market cannot name one of them.

There is nothing left to renew and nobody moving to renew it: the window opened, the chancery let the season pass, and the clerks entered that as a decision because there was nothing else to enter it as.

The {term} between {settlement} and {counterpart} still stands, re-cut rather than let go: a mediator sat the two courts down over a pact neither had broken, and the terms {settlement} argued itself hoarse over are the ones it keeps.

The town remarks that nothing was seized and nothing was burned: the renunciation was read out in the square, and the clerks defaulted the {term} before the square had emptied.
Courts have begun pricing what a promise out of {settlement} is worth, and they are pricing it low.
This house has disavowed {band} times before, and the entry has sat {timeband_since} in every chancery that keeps such entries.
The next proposal out of {settlement} will be refused on the credibility rather than on the terms, and there will be no arguing it, because there are no terms to argue.

The treaty with {counterpart} stands, and stands because nobody spoke: no word came from the new seat there and the date passed, which is what the law reads silence as, and {settlement}'s captains declined to believe it for as long as they were able.

lines.text: The rows against {counterpart} are in {settlement}'s book and are not counted when the hall counts {counterpart}: the war party can read them and cannot cite them, and the standing grievance reads {band} lighter for it.
The town has never stopped arguing about which cost more, the grain or the pride: the price was read out in the square before witnesses who will outlive the seat that swore it.
{settlement} will tell you the quarrel is buried. {counterpart} has buried nothing, and a decree binds only the hall that made it.
{faction} has waited in the open since the decree was read, and the elders here know the difference between a grudge that is closed and one that is merely uncited.
A later hall at {counterpart} cited the rows anyway, word for word, and {timeband_since} the old {wound} is back in {settlement}'s book with a new one on top of it for the revoking.

{counterpart} keeps its quarrel and {settlement} keeps the receipt: the price was paid in full against the wrong account (the carts went and were taken and thanked for), and the {temple} that witnessed the swearing has been asked about it twice since.
